chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Safwan from Umar ibn Rabah who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'When I arrive in Mecca, do I complete (the pilgrimage) or shorten (it)?' He said, 'Complete (it).'

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on completing or shortening prayers for a pilgrim arriving in Mecca?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who enters the Miqat or arrives in Mecca in a state where the time for shortening prayers (Qasr) has lapsed, directing them to perform Tamm (complete) prayers. This establishes the principle that the obligation of Tamm is tied to the specific temporal or ritual status at the point of entry, reflecting the juristic precision of the Imams in distinguishing between temporary and permanent states of pilgrimage. The ruling underscores the importance of adhering to the Imam's directive regarding the completeness of ritual acts when the conditions for concession (Qasr) are no longer met.
